title: Rapid coverage shift announcement playbook
content:
TL;DR:
We need to shift weekday coverage to a rapid-coverage pattern for the next 72 hours because of predicted capacity constraints in us-west-2 and the scheduled patching window. This doc is a lightweight announcement + Q&A + checklist to send to the all-eng and oncall channels. Keep tone calm, concrete, and explicitly state what we expect engineers to do (and not do).

Audience:
- Primary: Eng oncall, SRE rotations, platform and serving runtime engineers.
- Secondary: Product and support leads (FYI).

When to send:
- Draft message targeted for 10:30 PDT (before maintenance starts at 11:00 PDT).
- Follow up at T+1h with status update; T+12h summary; final restore message when back to normal.

Channels:
- Slack: #oncall, #serving-runtime, #platform-engineering (announce), #all-eng (FYI short note).
- Email: execs+managers list only if any SLA breach is imminent (do not spam execs unless needed).

Announcement script (short):
"Hi all — quick operations update. We’re shifting to a rapid-coverage oncall pattern for the next ~72 hours due to capacity headroom reductions in us-west-2 and a coordinated infra patching window.

What changes:
- Primary oncall remains unchanged.
- We’re adding a second responder rota (rapid-coverage) from 11:00 PDT today through 11:00 PDT in 3 days. Rapid-coverage tasks are limited to: triage, acknowledging page, applying documented fallbacks, and following escalation. No non-critical code deploys during this window.

What we need from engineers:
- If you are on the rapid-coverage rota: please monitor pages and confirm availability in #oncall within 15 minutes of this post.
- If you’re a service owner: double-check automatic fallback policies (see linked playbook) and ensure circuit-breakers are set to default values.
- If you had a deploy planned in the window: pause it unless it mitigates an incident.

We’ll post hourly status updates in #oncall. If you have questions, ping @Diego or @Mikaela. More details + checklist below."

Anticipated Q&A (prep answers):
Q: Why 72 hours?
A: Conservative window to cover the patching sequence and to observe post-patch behavior. We can shorten if telemetry is stable at checkpoints (T+12h, T+24h).

Q: Who is on the rapid rota?
A: Rapid rota is pulled from the normal oncall pool + an extra volunteer list. Current volunteers: Rowan, Aisha (backup), Priya (backup). (Note: confirm volunteers before publish.)

Q: Does this affect Dedicated/Private customers?
A: Hosted clusters in us-west-2 are impacted for capacity headroom. Dedicated and Private customers on isolated capacity are not impacted unless they rely on cross-region proxies; we’ll message CS separately if there’s any customer-facing impact.

Operational checklist (for publish + responders):
- Before 11:00 PDT: confirm rapid rota list and update rota page (Confluence) — @Rowan owns.
- 10:45 PDT: Send Slack announcement to #oncall and #platform-engineering.
- 11:00 PDT: First confirmation ping — responders acknowledge in #oncall.
- Hourly: Post short status note: successes, open pages, mitigations.
- If a page escalates to Sev2+: follow the standard incident flow (PROJ-4821) and inform SRE manager.
- No non-essential deploys: enforce via bake/CI gate comments and ask release owners to pause.
- Metrics to watch: avg token latency, GPU queue length, autoscale latency, error-rate-by-service (dashboards listed below).

Quick copy-paste status template (hourly):
"STATUS | T+{h} | Rapid coverage: {ok/concern} | open pages: {n} | latency: {p50/p95} | note: {short}"

Dashboards/links to monitor:
- Serving runtime overview: https://grafana.redwood/d/serving-runtime-overview
- GPU pool health: https://grafana.redwood/d/gpu-pool-health
- Autoscaler logs query: https://logs.redwood/query?q=autoscaler

Escalation path (short):
- Rapid responder -> Primary oncall -> SRE manager (Diego) -> Eng director (Mikaela).
- If customer-facing impact or billing alerts, loop in CS lead (Rina) and PM (Jonas).

Deploy pause checklist (for release owners):
- Cancel/delay any scheduled deploys during window (confirm in release channel).
- If deploy is emergency hotfix, include a short rollbook in the PR and coordinate with oncall.

Notes to selves / things to confirm before publish:
- [ ] Confirm volunteer list and update rota dashboard (Rowan).
- [ ] Verify linked Confluence playbook is up-to-date (remove stubs) — @Diego to check.
- [ ] Notify CS to pre-emptively hold any customer-facing messaging unless required.
- [ ] Create temporary incident Slack thread template for rapid triage (PR 87 references this).

Potential pitfalls / rough edges to call out in message (be transparent but avoid alarmism):
- There may be short-lived spikes in queue depth during rolling patches; we expect transient latency blips, not sustained errors.
- If autoscaler misbehaves, fallback is to scale a small reserve pool manually (SRE ops note included below).

SRE ops note (internal):
- Manual reserve procedure: 1) Authenticate to ops-console, 2) Spin up reserve GPU instances in us-west-2 using template 'reserve-small', 3) Attach to serving pool, 4) Watch queue drain; call MIKAELA when reserve is live (~15 min). (Write exact commands in Confluence playbook.)

Post-window followup (owner: Irene):
- T+72h: Publish short postmortem-style note in #platform-engineering summarizing what happened, metrics, and next steps.
- If any incidents occurred: open post-incident review ticket and link to incident timeline.

Draft Slack post (full):
"Heads up — operations update: we’re initiating a short rapid-coverage shift for the next ~72 hours (us-west-2 patching + reduced capacity). Primary oncall unchanged; an extra rapid responder rota will be active from 11:00 PDT today. Rapid responders: {list}.

Please: if you’re on the rota, ack in #oncall; service owners please double-check fallbacks; pause non-critical deploys. We’ll post hourly check-ins. Questions -> ping @Diego or @Mikaela. Full playbook: https://confluence.redwood/example-coverage-shift (internal)."

Tone guide (for author):
- Concise, non-alarmist, actionable. Lead with what changed and what engineers must do.
- Avoid blame; emphasize protections in place and who to contact.

Open items and TODOs:
- Confirm volunteer list (Rowan) — blocker for announcement.
- Small edit: replace placeholder Confluence link with live page after Diego updates it.
- Validate that scheduled batch jobs are not set to run heavy GPU workloads during the patch window (ask infra).

Hand-off notes (if I am not available):
- Diego has the rights to publish; Rowan will own rota updates; Mikaela will approve the final message.

-----
Draft ends. Save as small working doc; will iterate after volunteers confirmed.
